claims.statement: `memory_control` is an owner-facing read-and-act layer over the vault git tree, the disposable index and the append-only audit log; it deliberately introduces no second memory store, so every answer about what is remembered is derived from objects that already exist.

Memory control and client control are engine-host CLI owner surfaces, not MCP tools: `hypermnesic memory` and `hypermnesic clients` are dispatched from the CLI, while the server registers only the read tools plus `commit_note`, so a connected client cannot list its own grant, revoke a peer, or delete a memory.

The listing/inspect record is assembled field by field from its own source rather than from a stored summary: index membership supplies the path, `ingest.note_title` supplies frontmatter title then first H1 then de-kebabbed stem, the first indexed chunk supplies a 220-character snippet, `git log -1 --format=%H -- <rel>` supplies the last commit and its subject, the latest audit entry for that path supplies the actor (else the literal `unknown`), and the record carries `provenance` stated in file-and-commit terms (`source: git-file`, `path`, `last_commit`).

Source type is evidence-derived, not a stored label: `generated` when the text carries the `generated_by: hypermnesic` demarcation, `captured` when the path lives under the `sources/` prefix, `authored` otherwise.

`list_memories` filters by a normalized trailing-slash folder prefix, writability, source type, and recency, and reports honest degradation through `degraded_lexical_only` (index chunks with no dense vector) and `manual_reindex_recommended` (the index checkpoint is not at HEAD) instead of hiding it.

`inspect_memory` is bounded by index membership: a path outside the index's path set returns a `not_found` result with `error: "memory_not_found"`, and the record carries a bounded snippet with no full-body field, so reading a note stays a separate explicit act rather than a side effect of controlling it.

`write_scope` answers "what may an agent write?" from the same guard the write path enforces: folder entries come from `folders.derive_folders`, whose per-folder `writable` flag is `serialize.writable_reason(prefix + "__probe__.md", allowlist=...)`, so the reported answer cannot disagree with what `commit_note` accepts (including nested cases such as `projects/scripts/` being non-writable while `projects/` is writable).

The write-scope answer labels itself: `summary.mode` is `allowlist` when an allowlist was supplied and `blocklist` otherwise, because the CLI passes `--allowlist` through unchanged — an omitted flag therefore means the same blocklist default (protected-path refusals plus governance fence) that the engine runs with, and narrowing can only remove reach.

`export_memories` selects markdown by explicit `--path` or by folder listing, copies it preserving the relative layout, and writes `hypermnesic-export-manifest.json` carrying a version, an export timestamp, the filter that produced the selection, and per-file path, last commit, actor and source type; the status is `exported` or `empty`, and disposable index/state files are never copied.
Both destructive memory verbs preview by default and act only with `--apply`, and both land their effect as a git commit rather than a bare delete.

`apply_forget` executes in a fixed order — guard check, clean-tree preflight, acquire the single-indexer lock, `git rm -- <rel>`, a path-scoped `git commit -- <rel>`, removal of the path's index rows with a checkpoint advance, then one `forget` audit entry — releases the lock in a `finally`, and returns verification facts (does the source exist, does the index still contain the path, is a manual reindex recommended) plus the operation's own limits.

A refused forget leaves no partial effect: a protected path raises from the guard before the file is read or any git command runs, and a dirty tree raises before the git operation, which the focused tests assert by checking that HEAD and the target file are unchanged after each refusal.

`preview_revert` supports only commits that change exactly one markdown file and reports `commit_not_found` for an unresolvable commit; `apply_revert` raises rather than attempting a partial revert on an unsupported commit, aborts a failed `git revert` before raising, and on success re-projects the affected path (lexical upsert if present, row removal if not), advances the checkpoint, and appends one `revert` audit entry.

`audit_view` projects the append-only log onto a fixed safe shape (timestamp, actor, verb, attempted verb, path, old and new SHA, summary, category), returns the last N entries under `--limit`, re-redacts every summary through `_safe_summary` on read so redaction applies to all verbs, and treats a missing log file as an empty history rather than an error.

The audit log sets the actor itself and ignores a caller-supplied actor, truncates summaries to `MAX_SUMMARY` so note bodies cannot land in the file, is append-only (prior entries are never rewritten), and its reconciler back-fills `reconcile` entries for commits between the last logged `new_sha` and HEAD, making a crash between commit and append auditable rather than invisible.

Body-free refusal entries (`verb: "refusal"` with `attempted_verb` and a `category`) are a supported log shape that the audit view renders, but `append_refusal` has no production caller — the write path returns refusals to its caller instead of logging them and only the test suite appends refusal entries — so an audit view with no refusals means nothing recorded a refusal, not that nothing was refused.

The grant store is secret-free metadata by construction: every read and write projects each grant onto a fixed key allowlist (so a field outside it cannot be persisted even if supplied), `upsert_grant` requires a `grant_id` and replaces by that id, writes are atomic through a temporary file plus `os.replace`, grants are kept in a stable sort order, and a store with the wrong shape is refused loudly rather than reported as zero grants.

`clients revoke` previews by default and with `--apply` marks the stored grant revoked and inactive with a timestamp while returning a `next_effect` string that names the consequence; an unknown grant id returns `not_found` and an already-revoked grant returns `already_revoked`, so revocation is idempotent rather than failing on a repeat.

The OAuth provider writes and consults that same metadata store: it persists an issued grant's metadata (including `write_enabled` derived from whether `write` is in the granted scopes) through `client_control.upsert_grant`, and on each access-token validation and refresh it re-checks the store and, when the grant is marked revoked, drops the whole token family including the refresh sibling — so a revocation performed out of band takes effect on the next validation rather than only at the next restart.

The grant store defaults to `<repo>/.hypermnesic/client-grants.json` and is overridable with `--grant-store`, while restart-survivable live token material (client registrations and bearer/refresh tokens) lives in a separate owner-only `cloud-oauth-state.json` under the same state directory that is deliberately not a listing surface.

Write access is granted only when the owner approves the `write` scope at consent, and approval is not a bypass: the write tool self-enforces the scope per call (independently of the transport's global scope list) and returns `committed: false` with an `insufficient_scope` refusal stating that protected-path, frontmatter, dirty-tree, head-drift, audit and git-coordination guards still apply.

Unlike `commit_note`, which fetches, fast-forwards and pushes before finishing a write, `apply_forget` and `apply_revert` only create a local commit, so on a shared-remote deployment publishing the new commit remains the owner's responsibility.

Locking is asymmetric between the two destructive verbs: `apply_forget` holds the engine's single-indexer lock around the git removal and index update (released in a `finally`), whereas `apply_revert` takes no lock and relies on the clean-tree preflight plus the path-scoped `git revert`.

The `memory` command group converges the index before every read (with `--now` forcing a non-debounced pass), defaults to `<repo>/.hypermnesic/index.db` and `<repo>/.hypermnesic/audit.jsonl`, translates `FileNotFoundError`, `ValueError`, `WriteGuardError`, `DirtyTreeError` and `HeadDriftError` into a single stderr line with exit code 1, and leaves `LockBusyError` and `apply_revert`'s `RuntimeError` untranslated; `clients` translates `OSError` and `ValueError`. Every command in both groups supports `--json`.

`client_guidance.client_next_actions()` provides the secret-free client discovery list (local CLI, generic remote MCP client, Claude Code/Codex plugin, read-only Obsidian companion) whose `available` flag follows whether the install has a public URL, and both `doctor`/`status` and `setup` embed that same mapping so diagnosis and provisioning cannot disagree about the next client step.
